metadata.note: The Cheshire Railroad served the Monadnock region of southwestern New Hampshire (Keene and the Cheshire County seat, plus Troy and Winchendon), a gap in this map's New Hampshire coverage before now. Chartered in New Hampshire in 1844, it ran from a connection with the Vermont and Massachusetts Railroad at South Ashburnham, MA, through Winchendon, MA and Troy, NH, to Keene, NH (1848) and on to Bellows Falls, VT (Jan 1 1849) -- the first of four railroads to reach that town, linking the Fitchburg Railroad to the Vermont Central. Sold to the Fitchburg Railroad in 1890. Geometry is real-traced from OpenStreetMap (active rail combined with abandoned/disused railway tagging); every hop resolved to a connected, plausible real track path with no straight-line fallbacks needed.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheshire_Railroad (chartered NH 1844, consolidated with Winchendon Railroad 1845; South Ashburnham-Winchendon and Winchendon-Troy opened 1847; Keene 1848; Bellows Falls 1849; sold to Fitchburg Railroad September 3 1890)

https://www.unionleader.com/nh/voices/looking_back/1848-the-cheshire-railroad-connected-keene-to-boston/article_d979bf01-5ee2-47f2-b890-e9d02af827c3.html (July 1 1848: two round trips/day, Boston and Keene both at 7am/2pm, arriving 11am/6pm; Jan 1 1849 Cheshire RR first of four railroads to reach Bellows Falls)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap (via Overpass API, overpass.openstreetmap.fr mirror): railway=rail (active) combined with railway=abandoned/disused tagging, South Ashburnham MA to Bellows Falls VT via Winchendon, Troy, and Keene; routed via Dijkstra shortest path between each station's geocoded coordinates. All hops resolved to connected, plausible paths with no fallbacks needed.

Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
